changes: ce_approx refined to 1763/1764: Pauṣa of NS 884 falls in Dec 1763 or Jan 1764
Notes expanded: the lacunose verse is the stock yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā… lekhako doṣo na dīyate formula; 'śvala' is unexplained and may be part of the name or a Newari verb

notes: 'kunhu sidhayāṅā' (Newari) = 'completed on that day'. 'riṣitaṃ' = likhitam. The lacunose 'yā †dṛṣṭaṃ†… ṣo na dīyate' is the stock scribal verse (yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā … lekhako doṣo na dīyate), not a personal statement. 'śvala' after the scribe's name is unclear. It may be a corrupt Newari verb (e.g. 'wrote/finished') or part of the name. Era not stated; NS assumed because the script is Newari and the colophon is partly in Newari. NS 884 Pauṣa kṛṣṇa 14 ≈ Dec 1763/Jan 1764 CE.
